claims.wording: Pangalin Uninstaller is made by Pangalin, a trading name of KGB Equity (Pty) Ltd.
claims.excerpt: KGB Equity (Pty) Ltd ... trading as Pangalin

claims.wording: The vendor requires Apple silicon M1 or later and macOS 13 Ventura or later; Intel Macs are excluded.
claims.excerpt: a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 13 Ventura or later. It doesn't run on Intel Macs.

claims.wording: The current documented offer is free with every feature included, no account, ads or time limit; optional one-off support unlocks nothing.
claims.excerpt: No Pro, no licence, no account, no ads and no time limit. Everything Pangalin Uninstaller can do is free for everyone. ... Completely optional: it unlocks nothing ... A one-off payment, never a subscription
claims.conditions: Feature-specific hardware/OS requirements still apply. No licence means no paid activation licence, not absence of legal licence terms. Do not import Space Manager's 5 GB or $25 annual offer.

claims.wording: The newest release listed in the official history is 1.9.4, dated October 16, 2026.
claims.conditions: Release-history observation, not installed/downloaded version or execution test. Ignore the release history's macOS 27 readiness wording as untested vendor claims.

claims.wording: Pangolin Uninstaller is an acknowledged alternate spelling of the same Pangalin app.
claims.excerpt: if you searched for “Pangolin Uninstaller”, you're in the right place. It's the same app from the same two brothers.

claims.wording: Pangalin Space Manager is a distinct sibling storage app, not an alias for Uninstaller.
claims.excerpt: Pangalin Space Manager, our storage app, shows what's using your disk and helps you clean, move or compress it.

claims.wording: The documented uninstall/reset/leftovers workflow shows files before removal and normally moves selected files to Trash; Undo is limited to the most recent eligible removal.
claims.excerpt: Undo ... It's available until you quit the app, remove something else, or close the status line with ✕.
claims.conditions: Homebrew deletes the app, so Undo cannot restore it. Delete from Trash is permanent. Permission resets cannot be undone. System startup removals use a recoverable folder, not Trash. Modified items in Trash are not restored. Never promise every action is reversible.

claims.wording: Explain uses Apple Intelligence on-device and requires Apple silicon, macOS 26 and Apple Intelligence enabled; the control is hidden where unavailable.
claims.excerpt: Needs a Mac with Apple silicon running macOS 26 with Apple Intelligence turned on. Where it can't run, the button doesn't appear.
claims.conditions: EULA additionally conditions availability on supported language and region; explanations can be inaccurate and do not choose actions.

claims.wording: The vendor describes offline-by-default operation, with opt-in/manual update checks, optional Ask Apple too checks, Homebrew network caveats and clicked browser links.
claims.excerpt: Homebrew runs with its automatic updates and analytics switched off, but it's Homebrew's own program and may still go online.
claims.conditions: GitHub sees update-request IP/time. Do not call all operations permanently offline or claim independent privacy certification.

claims.wording: Full Disk Access is optional but limits scanning when absent; App Management is requested for uninstalling, and system-owned items use an optional helper with macOS approval covering five minutes.
claims.excerpt: One approval covers your removals and Undo for the next 5 minutes ... Full Disk Access is optional, but without it the app can't check some folders
claims.conditions: No settings or permissions changed here; no password accessed.

claims.wording: The official site says the app is notarised by Apple.
claims.conditions: No binary signature/notarization audit; never a guarantee of safety.

claims.wording: The app is offered under vendor-owned use terms, not an established open-source licence.
claims.excerpt: We own the apps and all rights in them. You get a licence to use them, not ownership.
claims.conditions: Personal, non-exclusive, non-transferable use on Macs personally owned or controlled; no screenshot publication grant identified.

claims.wording: The documented Startup and Trash-watcher features are not equivalent to CPU/memory helper grouping or recurring storage-growth monitoring.
claims.excerpt: It works while the app is open ... The Startup tab acts immediately
claims.conditions: Do not infer missing general monitoring features. Product-page release notes describe confirmation for Startup Remove, while EULA says Startup acts straight away without review list/Undo. Avoid exact confirmation promises until clarified.

claims.wording: Pangalin documents vendor-specific plug-in/model leftovers, offered conservatively, while explicitly excluding shared toolchains such as ~/.npm and ~/.cargo from its offers/inspection.
claims.excerpt: It never offers or looks inside key folders such as ~/.ssh, ~/.aws or ~/.gnupg, or shared toolchains such as ~/.npm or ~/.cargo.
claims.conditions: Not a measured completeness test, generic developer-cache cleanup claim or proof that all other paths are supported.

claims.wording: Breathing Room has documented storage views, grouped process inspection, activity and reviewable cleanup implementations; distributed-binary parity is unverified.
claims.excerpt: Source implementation is not proof that every feature works in the distributed installer.
claims.conditions: Free Apache-2.0 preview 0.1.0-preview.1, macOS 13+, universal installer advertised; physical Intel/clean-machine QA absent. Apple Development signed, not Developer ID signed/notarized. Python 3.10+ prerequisite.

claims.wording: Breathing Room advertises free local tools and optional AI Care at $5 USD/month or $50 USD/year; AI reasoning is authenticated and hosted.
claims.excerpt: AI Care is advertised at $5 USD/month or $50 USD/year ... Hosted AI assistance requires internet access and authentication
claims.conditions: Renewal/tax conditions apply; allowance/entitlement enforcement not verified. Relevant paths/process/storage data may reach service/Cloudflare. Website download account gate differs from direct GitHub release access. Daily care requires app running and saved exact approvals; optional automatic verified-Ruff mode qualifies blanket approval language.

workflow.title: Review Mac app leftovers without discarding shared plug-ins or AI models
workflow.primaryIntent: Decide whether app-scoped leftovers are expendable, shared or personal data before uninstalling a creative or AI app.
workflow.descriptionDirection: Explain why a small app bundle can own large shared or user-created data; use Pangalin's documented review workflow without pretending Breathing Room replaces its uninstaller.
outline: Identify the app, installation method and backup before removal
Read paths, sharing notes and unticked plug-ins/models rather than treating size as permission
Separate uninstall, reset, Homebrew and permanent Trash actions
Distinguish ongoing disk-growth investigation from app removal
Choose Pangalin for verified app-removal needs; consider Breathing Room, which we build, for broader investigation subject to preview/hosted/runtime caveats
workflow.visualPlan: Official review-sheet link identifies desired top visual but requires clearance/download/inspection. Selected Breathing Room Space preview later, preserving example-data labels.
workflow.interactionHandoff: Non-mutating decision checklist: keep app? shared plug-in/model/user work? package-manager install? current backup? No deletion commands, filesystem access or invented savings calculator.
workflow.length: Earned, normally 900–1800 words after gates clear
